source.historical_source: J. H. Conway, Five $1,000 Problems, OEIS50-DIMACS Conference (2014), updated 2017, OEIS A248380
source.normalized_statement: Does a finite simple graph on 99 vertices exist in which adjacent pairs have exactly one common neighbor and nonadjacent pairs have exactly two common neighbors?

lean_semantics.adjacent_clause: G.LocallyLinear, documented and used here as every adjacent pair lying in a unique triangle
lean_semantics.nonadjacent_clause: Pairwise over distinct vertices: not adjacent implies the intersection of neighbor sets has ncard exactly 2
lean_semantics.answer_wrapper: answer(sorry) makes this a yes/no existence question; a positive witness or impossibility proof is required, not a single failed candidate

literature_gate.current_reference: P. G. Cesarz and A. J. Woldar, On the automorphism group of a putative Conway 99-graph, Algebraic Combinatorics 8 (2025), 379-398, DOI 10.5802/alco.418; explicitly states existence remains open.
literature_gate.automorphism_obstruction: H. A. Wilbrink, On the (99,14,1,2) strongly regular graphs, EUT-Report 84-WSK-03 (1984), 342-355: a putative graph has no automorphism of order 11 and is not vertex-transitive.
literature_gate.spectral_data: A putative adjacency matrix has eigenvalues 14^1, 3^54, (-4)^44; Laplacian nonzero eigenvalues 11^54 and 18^44.

algebraic_reduction.matrix_identity: For n vertices, adjacency matrix A and degree diagonal D, the two common-neighbor clauses give A^2 = D - A + 2J - 2I.
algebraic_reduction.degree_sum_identity: Multiplying by the all-ones vector gives A d = 2(n-1) 1.
algebraic_reduction.regularity_argument: If delta and Delta are minimum and maximum degrees, evaluating the neighbor-degree sum at delta- and Delta-degree vertices gives delta*Delta=2(n-1). Equality forces min-degree vertices to neighbor only max-degree vertices and conversely. Connectedness follows from mu=2; if delta<Delta the graph would be bipartite, contradicting lambda=1 triangles. Hence delta=Delta=k.

quotient_and_transformation_gate.seed: Conway9 = K3 box K3, with exact parameters (9,4,1,2)
quotient_and_transformation_gate.candidate_transformation: A connected regular cyclic 11-sheet voltage lift of Conway9, followed by at most 12 ordinary degree-preserving 2-switches.
quotient_and_transformation_gate.why_this_is_the_exact_natural_quotient_t: The sheet count is forced by 99/9=11; a regular voltage lift is the standard replayable realization of Conway9 as a quotient, and 2-switches are the bounded catalogue operation that can break local common-neighbor structure while preserving order and degrees.
quotient_and_transformation_gate.obstruction_1: Every graph cover preserves the base degree, so every lifted vertex has degree 4. Every ordinary 2-switch preserves the full degree sequence. All outputs therefore remain 4-regular, while the target equations force 14-regularity.
quotient_and_transformation_gate.obstruction_2: Before any switches, a cyclic 11-lift has a deck automorphism of order 11, a domain excluded for every putative Conway99 graph by Wilbrink. Switches can break that symmetry but cannot repair the pinned degree coordinate.
quotient_and_transformation_gate.other_standard_blowups: The independent 11-blowup has degree 44 and the clique 11-blowup has degree 54, so neither supplies the required quotient either.

stop.reason: The exact quotient-derived lift/switch family exists but is algebraically pinned at degree 4, so no member can satisfy or even move the forced degree-14 target coordinate. The known 9-vertex analogue is an equation analogue, not an admissible quotient seed for this transformation.
stop.future_requirement: A future Phase 0 must first provide an explicit 99-vertex 14-regular quotient template with no order-11 deck symmetry and exact pairwise common-neighbor update equations; it may not retune this closed Conway9 lift/switch family.
